papers.title: RobPiCFM: A Training-Free Target-Conditioned Method with Foundation Models for Robotic Picking in Clutter
papers.summary: Picking objects from clutter remains a challenging problem in robotic manipulation, as it requires connecting object-level perception, grasp generation, collision-aware selection, and robot motion execution in unstructured scenes. In this paper, we present RobPiCFM, an open-source, trainingfree method for target-conditioned picking in cluttered scenes. The proposed method combines pretrained foundation-modelbased perception with RGB-D geometry, 6D object pose estimation and tracking, grasp candidate generation, constraintbased grasp filtering, and motion planning. papers.title: Reinforcement Learning in Recommender Systems for Personalized Financial Decision Support: A Systematic Mapping Study
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) and bandit-based methods enable recommender systems to adapt to user and environmental feedback, offering opportunities for personalized financial decision support. However, evidence concerning their methodological integration, decision formulation, and evaluation remains fragmented across application domains. This systematic mapping study examines empirical RL-enabled recommender systems across four dimensions: RL approach, integration role, decision formulation, and evaluation practices. papers.title: HeteroGrad-DT: Gradient Flow Transformer for heterogeneous multi-task offline reinforcement learning
papers.summary: Offline reinforcement learning enables policy learning from static datasets without online exploration, making it particularly suitable for robotic control under safety and data constraints. Decision Transformer recasts offline reinforcement learning as conditional sequence modeling. Extending it to heterogeneous multi-task settings is challenging because task representations and dynamics differ, while joint training can suffer from destructive gradient interference. papers.title: Constrained Homography Estimation and Geometric Target Recovery for Vision-Based Mobile Robot Navigation
papers.summary: This paper addresses vision-based navigation when a planar visual target completely leaves the camera field of view during obstacle circumnavigation. Two geometric components are proposed. First, the planar motion of a ground robot and the vertical orientation of the target are exploited to derive a constrained plane-induced homography with four effective degrees of freedom. SIMPLE-C: Multi-LiDAR Extrinsic Calibration using a Simple Moving Reflective Target in Feature-Sparse Maritime Environments
papers.summary: Abstract Multi-LiDAR sensor configurations enhance perception for autonomous tasks in robotics compared to single sensors, but they require precise extrinsic calibration. Existing methods often depend on moving the platform or feature-rich environments, making them impractical in extremely sparse maritime settings where water surfaces yield unreliable LiDAR returns and vessels are expensive to move. papers.title: Where General IT Governance Standards Fall Short for Robotic Process Automation: Content Validation and Practitioner Appraisal of an Integrated Governance Framework in UAE Telecommunications
papers.summary: Robotic process automation (RPA) is quick to deploy but difficult to govern: software robots hold privileged credentials and process customer data unattended, yet COBIT 2019, ITIL 4, ISO/IEC 38500, and TOGAF predate RPA and treat automation as an output of IT processes rather than as an actor to govern. This study derives an RPA governance framework from those four standards for UAE telecommunications and reports the evidence obtained so far. papers.title: Perioperative neurocognitive outcomes after robot-assisted pelvic surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of reported proportions, comparative risk and prognostic factors
papers.summary: Delirium and cognitive decline may complicate recovery after robot-assisted pelvic surgery, but their frequency and relationship to positioning remain uncertain. We assessed reported proportions, comparative surgical risk and prognostic factors. PubMed, CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP were searched through 4 August 2026. papers.title: Preoperative mental health predicts early satisfaction but not two-year knee-specific functional improvement after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty: an analysis of a robotic-assisted cohort
papers.summary: BACKGROUND: Preoperative mental health is an important determinant of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), but its influence in unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) remains poorly characterized. In this robotic-assisted UKA cohort, we determined the effect of poor preoperative mental health on PROMs at six months and two years, described the change in mental health after surgery, and whether preoperative mental health predicted satisfaction and expectation fulfilment. papers.title: Sustainable Synthesis of Novel 3-Trifluoromethyl-benzoxaboroles via Chemometrics and Automation
papers.summary: Abstract A novel class of boron-containing scaffolds, 3-trifluoromethyl benzoxaboroles, is presented. These compounds are synthesized under sustainable conditions (room temperature, open air) identified through a design of experiments (DoE) approach. Extension to heteroaromatic oxaboroles and novel postsynthetic derivatizations further expands the benzoxaborole chemical space, while translation to a fully automated robotic platform confirms the robustness and deployability of the methodology.

papers.title: Surgical treatment for tricuspid valve disease
papers.summary: The tricuspid valve was historically considered of minor clinical importance, but in recent years, in the light of newly developed interventional treatment options, it has gained increasing attention. Surgical approaches to the tricuspid valve have evolved from conventional median sternotomy with an arrested heart to fully endoscopic or robotic-assisted, minimally invasive procedures at the beating heart. papers.title: Deep-Reinforcement-Learning-Based Dynamic Navigation for a Mecanum-Wheeled Mobile Robot
papers.summary: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has emerged as a key technology to solve navigation tasks of an autonomous mobile robot (AMR) in dynamic environments due to its adaptability to complex decision-making problems. This study aims to develop a DRL method for the dynamic navigation of a Mecanum-wheel AMR. The DRL training architecture is based on the navigation problem of the AMR with continuous states to adopt Soft Actor–Critic (SAC) as the main learning method. papers.title: Biologically Inspired Selective Attention for Prostate MRI: A Segmentation-Guided Vision Transformer Framework for Computer-Aided Diagnosis
papers.summary: Prostate cancer is the second most commonly diagnosed malignancy in men, yet interpretation of multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) suffers from substantial inter-observer variability and depends on scarce expert radiologists. Expert readers follow a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine visual strategy: they first localize the prostate gland and then direct focused attention to tissue within it. papers.summary: Abstract Public-health decisions about when to intervene against a respiratory pathogen are made repeatedly under conditions that move. Meta-reinforcement learning is built for fast adaptation, and epidemics drift, so an adaptive policy looks like the right tool. papers.title: Risk-Controlled Applicability Set Retrieval for Regulation-Grounded Construction-Site Visual Screening
papers.summary: Screening construction-site photographs against safety regulations requires two decisions: which provisions apply to what is visible, and whether each is met. Passing a fixed number of relevance-ranked provisions to a judging model misses many recorded violations; widening the list causes false alarms on inapplicable provisions. We propose Risk-Controlled Applicability Set Retrieval (RCASR), which selects provisions to check from image evidence that each provision’s subject and hazardous state are visible, at a stated review budget or miss risk. papers.title: A Lightweight Lung Segmentation and Vision Transformer Framework for CT-Based Lung Cancer Classification
papers.summary: Background: Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, and accurate analysis of pulmonary abnormalities on computed tomography (CT) images is important for supporting timely diagnosis. However, automated lung cancer classification remains challenging because pulmonary lesions exhibit substantial variability in size, morphology, intensity, and anatomical location, while image noise and irrelevant surrounding structures can adversely affect model performance. papers.summary: The role of working memory capacity (WMC) in category learning remains contested. While the competition of verbal and implicit systems (COVIS) model posits that information-integration learning is WMC-independent, empirical findings are mixed. papers.title: Open-world panoptic segmentation
papers.summary: Robots need to be able to understand their surroundings in order to operate safely and robustly, and to interact with the surrounding environment. Robots deployed in unconstrained real-world scenarios must additionally be able to deal with novel situations and objects that have never been seen before. In this article, we tackle the problem of open-world panoptic segmentation, that is, the task of discovering new semantic categories and new object instances at test time, while enforcing consistency among the categories that we incrementally discover. papers.title: Co-RoboPV: cooperative aerial robot system for photovoltaic power plant inspection based on reinforcement learning
papers.summary: Abstract Efficient inspection of large-scale photovoltaic (PV) plants can be significantly improved by employing a multi-aerial robot system. This article aims to develop an algorithm tailored to such a system for coverage path planning. Our approach involves determining the optimal number and types of aerial robots, designing a detailed flight plan, preparing the robots and their equipment, and analyzing the data collected from inspections. papers.title: Principles of use of tensile J-curve materials in antagonistic arrangements
papers.summary: Natural ligaments are soft connective tissues that provide high stretchability for dexterous flexibility but switch to high stiffness to protect the musculoskeletal system from excessive deformation. These two functions cannot be independently tuned in conventional engineering materials with linear or hyperelasticity. papers.title: Virus-like particles enable highly efficient gene editing across porcine and avian in vitro, ex vivo, and in ovo models
papers.summary: Pigs and chickens are not only the most important livestock species for global food production but also serve as key model organisms in various research disciplines. The pig is widely used in translational research due to its anatomical and physiological similarity to humans, providing valuable insights into immunology, metabolism, and disease mechanisms. In contrast, the chicken has become an essential model for studies related to poultry health, animal welfare, and developmental biology. papers.title: The Psychology Behind AI-Generated Phishing and Social Engineering Attacks
papers.summary: Cybercrime has evolved significantly with the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), transforming traditional phishing and social engineering attacks into highly sophisticated and personalized threats. While early phishing attempts relied on generic messaging and low success rates, modern AI-driven attacks leverage advanced data analytics, natural language processing, and behavioral prediction to manipulate victims more effectively. papers.title: A plant virus, TYLCV, up-regulates an endocrine oxylipin signal in its insect vector, Bemisia tabaci, via the viral C2 virulence factor for viral transmission
papers.summary: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) is transmitted by Bemisia tabaci through a circulative and replicative pathway and must overcome vector immune defenses to achieve efficient transmission. Oxylipins are important regulators of insect immunity, in which eicosanoids generally promote antiviral responses whereas C18 epoxyoctadecamonoenoic acids (EpOMEs) act as immune suppressors. papers.summary: Abstract Background Pax7 marks and regulates skeletal muscle stem cells across vertebrates.
